title: Extend Go HTTP items server with full CRUD, pagination, and filtering in 3 steps
description: Multi-step Go task: take an HTTP server that only lists empty items, and build it into a full items CRUD API with in-memory store, pagination, and category/name filtering.

task_spec.prompt:
The existing server at internal/handler/items.go has only a stub ListItems that returns {"items": []}. Evolve it in 3 steps.

Step 1 — In-memory store + full CRUD:
  Add to internal/handler/items.go:
    type Item struct { ID int; Name string; Category string; Price float64 } (json tags)
    var items []Item + var nextID = 1 + var mu sync.Mutex
    func ResetItems()              — clear store (for tests)
    func ListItems(w, r)           — GET /items → {"items": [...], "total": N} (keep existing signature)
    func CreateItem(w, r)          — POST /items, JSON body → 201 + created item; 400 if Name empty
    func GetItem(w, r)             — GET /items/{id} → 200 + item; 404 if missing

Step 2 — Pagination:
  ListItems must honour ?limit=N&offset=M query params.
  Return full list (no pagination) if params absent.
  Slicing: result[offset:min(offset+limit, len)] — clamp to bounds.

Step 3 — Filtering:
  ListItems must also honour:
    ?category=X  — case-insensitive equality filter on Category
    ?q=keyword   — case-insensitive substring filter on Name
  Filters apply before pagination.

Update cmd/server/main.go to register:
  /items   → GET→ListItems, POST→CreateItem
  /items/  → GetItem

All existing fixture tests (TestListItems) plus new solution tests must pass.
Run: go test ./...
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `go test ./...` to see where we stand. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.
Final push: run `go test ./...` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure the full implementation is complete and all tests pass.
